Mmhmm. Checking my playtime now, 2013 ran me 8 hours (with some of the optional stuff and a tad of multiplayer), and Rise ran me 16 (again some optional stuff on the side). I'm not really a completionist, so you should get at least what I have and then some. Even more with the DLCs if you opt to buy them as well, but I'm not sure how much content they give in terms of achievements and collectibles.

Regarding MGS, to be honest, I obviously think they're best played. You get to piece together the story yourself, and also enjoy some pretty decent games. That said, if you don't have another console to buy them for etc, I'd probably recommend watching this analysis/review of the games themselves. I've seen a few videos he's done, and I've seen these as well, and I'd say they're pretty good overview of each game. That said it's not particularly quick - he basically plays the whole game, and abridges it into 40 minutes a piece. The MGS4 video is actually 1hr 20, although I wouldn't bother with it, as the events of MGS4 are the last to occur in the entire MGS timeline, and so you wouldn't be missing much if you were to skip it. You could arguably skip Peace Walker as well, but if you choose to watch the main 3, I'd throw in Peace Walker for good measure. The reason I would recommend watching these over say 'entire MGS in 5 mins' is because this at least brushes over all of the content in each of the games, rather than just cherry picking the best bits. It's ultimately up to you, but if you're not going to play, you might as well essentially watch the game first hand. No reason for an LP though. I also wouldn't recommend reading the Wiki, but I was never the type to read books.

In regards to your repetitive comment - hmmmm, yeah. The best way to describe MGSV is that it's a great game, but not a good Metal Gear game.

I still recommend only buying it if you're a fan of the series. If you watch that playlist and still aren't 100% interested, the game'll be a paperweight in your library.
